clue.text: Scoundrel is banished from north of Scottish island, getting the bird

indicators.note: in this clue the first piece is placed above, so before, the second

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

indicators.note: the word is is thrown out of the island's name

parts.note: Lewis is the northern part of the Outer Hebridean island of Lewis and Harris
the clue word is gives the two letters removed

explanation.surface: A villain is expelled from a northern Scottish island and jeered by the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' looks like being booed; it is the definition. In an across clue 'north of' just means the scoundrel comes first; LEWIS is in the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a long-billed wading bird of moors and shores.

the answer is tucked away inside the words lean lurcher

clue.text: In Irish province, establish church for new royal favourite

indicators.note: the church abbreviation goes in place of the letter for new

parts.note: Leinster is one of the four provinces of Ireland
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Instructions to found a church in an Irish province for a new favourite of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the usual abbreviation for new; CE replaces it in LEINSTER. 'In' and 'establish' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was famously a favourite of Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Sardonic about male Republican's 13

parts.note: wry means drily mocking

explanation.surface: A cynical remark about a Republican man.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 points to the answer of 13 across, BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge, a type of boat.

clue.text: Serve as vessel holding last of beer for capital chap

indicators.note: the phrase made of the two pieces keeps a letter held inside it

a liner is a large passenger ship

indicators.note: only the final letter of beer is wanted

explanation.surface: A tankard of beer is offered to a man from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve as' gives BE, and the R from 'beer' goes into the gap between the two words, so the vessel is split by nothing but sits after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a man from Berlin, the German capital.

clue.text: Sensational clanger? Poor don had to go into it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside the mistake

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' scrambles DON HAD TO into OODANDTH, which 'go into' the BLUNDER; 'it' points back to the clanger.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-and-thunder describes melodramatic, sensational entertainment full of violence.

clue.text: Got up to deliver plant in this?

parts.note: rose is the past of rise, to get up
in cricket, to bowl is to deliver the ball

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to hand over a plant pot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball; the definition is a container you might plant a rose in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a bowl for displaying roses, a vessel for the flower.

clue.text: One competed to be covered with 8

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Someone entered a contest to be draped in greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, EVERGREEN; ivy is an evergreen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied means covered in ivy, a climbing evergreen.

clue.text: Scots pine, perhaps, when English politician secures rise for minister

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A Scottish tree stands as a minister rises with an English politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots pine' looks like a native tree to find; it is an example of the definition. 'rise for' turns the minister upwards in this down clue; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots pine is a conifer that keeps its leaves all year, an example of such trees.

clue.text: Native record company receiving good intelligence

explanation.walkthrough: An indie label is an independent record company, not one of the big majors.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous peoples are those native to a place, born and rooted there.

clue.text: Day in mid-month that is endless!

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell on the 13th or 15th, the middle of the month.

clue.text: Judge slipped up —— appealed against

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.definitionFit: A decision referred to a higher authority is one sent up for review, as when it is challenged.

clue.text: Bloke keen, some say, to establish wine-shop

indicators.note: the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: bod is slang for a bloke, and keen means eager

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic man is eager to open a wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD EAGER said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar bar.

clue.text: Club adopting old cat, for example

indicators.note: the club takes a letter in as its own

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: A club takes in an elderly cat as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' looks like a pet; it is a catboat, a small sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat, or catboat, is a kind of small sailing vessel with one mast set far forward.

clue.text: Go too far with regard to project

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning
to shoot is to send out or project

explanation.surface: Advice not to overreach on a project.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to pass beyond a target, going further than intended.

clue.text: Information from all quarters, with authentic sound

parts.note: the four compass points are north, east, west and south, N E W S

explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns REAL into its sound-alike REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short film of current events shown in cinemas, a form of information.

clue.text: Laid off and turned out

indicators.note: the letters of and turned are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker was dismissed and shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like a second definition; 'turned' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the anagram of AND TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant workers are dismissed because their jobs are no longer needed.

clue.text: Fabric absorbing moisture on a footpath

clue.text: Unsightly appearance of faces, excluding 1,000 without wrinkles
